newsitem.title: USA: Air Force approves resuming Delta-2 launches.
newsitem.headline: Air Force approves resuming Delta-2 launches.

text.p: The U.S. Air Force said on Wednesday it had approved resuming commercial Delta-2 rocket launches by McDonnell Douglas Corp. from Vandenberg Air Force Base, Calif., and Cape Canaveral Air Station, Fla.

Approval by the Air Force Space Command followed a study and safety steps taken after the failure of a Delta-2 launched from Cape Canaveral on Jan. 17. That rocket was carrying an Air Force global positioning satellite.
Friday's next commercial space launch of a Delta is now set to carry five IRIDIUM satellites for cellular telephone communications into space from Vandenberg at 8:12 a.m. Pacific time (1512 GMT).
A second Delta-2 rocket, scheduled to be launched from Cape Canaveral on May 11, will carry a Norweigan Thor-2A communications satellite into space.
The Air Force Space Command, located at Colorado Springs, Colo., said that "McDonnell Douglas and its contractor team have taken numerous actions for a safe return to flight."
"Based on its review and the actions the Air Force and the contractor team have taken, the Air Force is confident the Delta-2 can return to flight," the command said in a statement.
